findings.detail: Ranks 18-20 are out of order by the stated metric (miles descending). MD=31 mi is ranked 18, above AL=53 mi (rank 19) and MS=44 mi (rank 20). Correct descending order should be AL (53), MS (44), then MD (31).
Rank 15 AR=53,179 sq mi is placed above rank 16 IA=56,273 sq mi. IA is larger and should be ranked ahead of AR.

AK listed as on the Continental Divide of the Americas (Brooks Range). The Continental Divide of the Americas as commonly defined ends at Cape Prince of Wales area; the Brooks Range hosts the Arctic Divide, not the Continental Divide of the Americas. Disclaimer even acknowledges 'five contiguous states plus Alaska' — inconsistent framing.

Values are trail-miles (1,700 mi / 455 mi / 506 mi) but ranks follow geographic south-to-north order, not descending mileage. If ranked by miles, order would be CA, WA (506), OR (455). Mixing an ordered rank with an unrelated metric is confusing.

Numerous ranks are not in descending mi order. Examples: rank 15 AL=905 above rank 16 VA=1,118; rank 20 WY=913 above rank 21 MT=1,192; rank 27 NM=1,000 above rank 26 AR=743 (OK) but rank 31 AZ=1,169 sits below rank 15 AL=905; rank 37 UT=938 below rank 35 NE=482. The entire back half of the list is scrambled relative to the stated 'longest to shortest' ordering.

Multiple ranks violate descending order. Examples: rank 17 KS=138 above rank 12 MN=123 by value but ranked lower; rank 33 MT=119 above rank 11 IN=127 by value; rank 25 AR=90 above rank 22 AL=85; rank 36 ND=89 above rank 34 ID=82. The tail of the list is not sorted by airport count.

Ranks not in descending bridge-count order. Examples: rank 15 MN=13,477 above rank 16 VA=13,900; rank 17 MS=17,068 (would rank ~13); rank 19 AL=16,151 (would rank ~14); rank 26 NE=15,364 (would rank ~15). Multiple states in the middle of the list have counts exceeding states ranked far above them.

CO=5,281 peaks is identical to CO=5,281 summits reported in the sibling 'Most Named Mountain Peaks' question (all GNIS summits regardless of elevation). It's implausible that 100% of Colorado's GNIS-named summits are above 5,000 ft — value appears copied from the other question rather than filtered by elevation.
Rank 25 IA=8,500 acres is placed above rank 26 MS=35,000 acres and neighbors. IA at 8,500 acres should rank far lower (roughly rank 32), and MS/TX/LA etc. above it should shift up.
